overview: Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn appeared on Medford Happenings to discuss the city's legal representation, defend recent labor litigation settlements, and address the City Council's decision to cut the legal department's budget.

items.title: Guest Introduction
items.summary: Host John Petrella introduced Mayor Breanna Lungo-Koehn for a discussion on city services and administrative challenges.

items.title: City Legal Representation and KP Law
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn defended the administration's decision to contract with municipal law firm KP Law, explaining that having access to their specialized attorneys has helped advance city ordinances and the redevelopment of Medford Square.

items.title: Labor Litigation and Settlements
items.summary: The Mayor detailed three employment labor lawsuits filed against the city, explaining her decision to defend the cases and resolve two of them with settlements of $19,000 and $28,000 to protect the city from larger financial demands.

items.title: City Council Relationship and Budget Cuts
items.summary: Mayor Lungo-Koehn stated that the City Council cut the municipal legal budget by 83% in June, and she characterized their ongoing inquiries into litigation costs as political maneuvering ahead of the next mayoral election.

items.title: Bond Rating and Legal Spending Comparison
items.summary: The Mayor reported that the city successfully maintained its high bond rating after the rating agency dismissed local litigation concerns as political noise, and she shared data showing Medford's legal expenses are lower than those of neighboring communities.

items.title: Show Conclusion
items.summary: Petrella concluded the interview, thanked the Mayor, and provided information on how to access replays and podcasts of the program.
